summary: Processes: a set of interrelated actions and activities performed to achieve a specified set of products, results, or services. Good processes, meaning those based on sound principles and proven practices, are project managers' best friends. They act like the solid tracks that keep a train going in the direction it needs to go. Following a set of established processes minimizes confusion and uncertainty for the project manager and all project stakeholders. It ensures the effective progress of the project from initiation through to close-out. In this course, learners will be given an overview of the project management process groups as defined in A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK®) Guide – Fourth Edition published by the Project Management Institute (PMI®). Program Description:

Most of us go through life believing that it will be a smooth ride. And when it's not we say it's fate - it has been decided that way! Then we secretly want to alter our 'fate' by hoping and wishing we will strike it lucky one day. Or we totally succumb to our 'fate' that we feel jealous about others who drive a nice car and live in a nice house. We start blaming and pointing fingers. Little do we know that there motivational self improvement called “The Winning Edge”

Worse some wish they were born in rich families or hope one day to win a lottery or hit a jackpot at the casino. They have never heard of living life by design...They don't know life is not lived by wishing and hope alone. They don't know you can craft it, to your liking! Sadly a person in this predicament has not the slightest idea how to motivate themselves into self improvement. They think they are born like that. It is in their DNA, unless something dramatic happens in their life.

Everyone wants to be successful. But to be successful, there is an important thing you must have and that is Winning Edge.

SE, SSE, TL

    • Believe in your self

Course Full Name: Evolution of Technology in Travel Industry
summary:
Travel Technology or Hospitality Automation is the term used for defining application of IT in the Travel & Tourism Industry.

Travel Technology was originally associated with Computer Reservation Systems (CRS). In 1946, American Airlines installed the first automated booking system, the experimental electromechanical Reservisor and soon replaced it with temporary storage based on a magnetic drum, the Magnetronic Reservisor. The new product was used by several Airlines as well as Sheraton Hotels and Goodyear for inventory control. Initial developments were a start however they were labor intensive and lacked remote access.

summary:
PharmacyRx is a networked application. With a networked application, a large computer (based at McKesson) stores your pharmacy information such as patient, product, and prescriber data, and runs the software that allows you to fill prescriptions. You access the software through a fast and secure connection on the company’s network using an internet browser. The information stored at McKesson’s central computer is extremely secure, more secure than if it were stored at your pharmacy!

McKesson’s server facility offers a level of protection and security far beyond what would be available at a pharmacy level, including:

a. A highly secure SSL (Secure Socket Layer) that protects your data as it travels over the Web

b. Redundant storage of data on several minor systems to ensure security and availability

c. Highly sophisticated firewalls that restrict access to data

d. Intrusion detection systems that increase protection

e. Physical facility designed to withstand forces of nature

f. A three-stage system that provides continuous power

g. Over 100 closed-circuit cameras monitoring entire facility

h. Server access restricted to authorized personnel only using powerful authentication software

Description

Many Project Managers have a true love-hate relationship with Microsoft project. It gets a bad rep, mainly, because it’s not understood well. Most of the time, when we see an ‘unexpected result’ in using the tool, the result is only unexpected because we don’t know the tool well enough to predict its behavior. The purpose of this series will be to demystify MS Project, and create a much more enjoyable experience in its use as we understand it better.

This session will present background and key knowledge one must have to begin the journey with MS Project. For many, it will be a refresher course, but for others the very understanding of basic terminology and approaches will start the path to your ‘lights-on’ moment !

In future sessions, we will build out a fully functional schedule which will be used to walk through the steps of managing a project with this powerful tool. Along the way, many of the ‘quirks’ and ‘pitfalls’ of MS Project will be discussed.

Duration

45 Minutes

Training Mode

Recorded Webinar

This webinar was presented by Elaine Lee at NTT DATA’s Design Week event that took place from March 9-15, 2015.  

This webinar focuses on the concepts of Design Empathy and Design Prototyping.  I'll be exploring how design empathy can be achieved through 'needs finding' and should be leveraged to design for people and the needs of people as a way to drive a customer centric ideation process.  I'll share a process I recently used with a client that demonstrates how it can be done.  Design empathy can be introduced into projects even if the entire Design Thinking process lifecycle is not being implemented. 

I'll also talk about the importance of prototyping and testing in Design Thinking.  We will explore why prototypes aren't what you build after you have an idea, but it's what you do to create the idea.  We will discuss how prototyping can be used to build your way forward to develop and enhance your ideas.

Course Full Name: Design Thinking In The World Of IoT
summary: Description:  Explore the importance and best practices of Design Thinking in the world of IoT    Synopsis:  Just because you can, does not mean you should. That seems to be the big lesson learnt from early IoT startups. Consumers are rejecting novel technology ideas and do not seem to connect to IoT. They are sometimes accepting IoT applications in their own way, and not as designed. Where are the designers going wrong? Is technology part of the problem or the user mindset is?  We will explore answers to these questions and learn about the importance and techniques of design thinking which can be used for developing IoT products and applications. We will also take some examples and observe how different aspects of design thinking can improve different areas of IoT design and development.    Presenter:  Arushi Srivastava

Course Full Name: AI Everywhere – What Are The Consequences?
summary: Description:  Artificial Intelligence – How is AI permeating every Industry & what are the consequences  Synopsis:  AI is still an emerging technology. A disruptor. It can be seen ‘behind the scenes’ everywhere these days – from search engines to mobile apps, to soft robots automating knowledge work, to even AI that occupy corporate board positions.   In this talk we explore the key accelerating technology trends shaping our society and explore the convergence of these trends that is bringing AI into prominence. Focusing on some of the key emerging trends in AI – machine learning, deep learning, natural language and image processing, we outline how AI is impacting various sectors in financial services, healthcare, technology, entertainment and media, consumer and industrial products, and retail. The rapid advances in AI have resulted in a big VC investment followed by large acquisitions of start-ups by incumbent players around the globe. Social consequences of AI range from it being an existential threat to mankind, to creating massive job losses and social unrest in the next decade, to a ‘hype’ that will go away in a year. We explore the evidence behind these viewpoints and conclude by discussing what individuals should be doing to be more relevant in an AI-dominated world, what companies should be doing to continue to be viable and profitable, and what countries should be doing to economically and socially thrive  Presenter:  Anand Rao

summary: Program Description:    How often have you used brainstorming to solve a problem? Chances are, you've used it at least once, even if you didn't realize it. For decades, people have used brainstorming to generate ideas, and to come up with creative solutions to problems. Brainstorming is a way to generate ideas within a group setting. It is usually used in the beginning stages of a project, where the possibilities for the project are not clearly understood or defined. It provides a quick means for tapping the creativity of a limited number of people for a large number of ideas. The brainstorming environment fosters an uninhibited, non-judgmental explosion of ideas, concepts, policies, decisions, and strategies. In brainstorming, all contributions are valid, and the key to a successful session is to share as many ideas as possible without evaluating them. Brainstorming combines a relaxed, informal approach to problem solving with lateral thinking. It encourages people to come up with thoughts and ideas which can be crafted into original, creative solutions to a problem, while others can spark even more ideas. This helps to get people unstuck by "jolting" them out of their normal ways of thinking.    Objectives:    At the end of this Brainstorming Techniques Training Course, participants will be able to:    Describe the techniques of effective brainstorming  Identify and use common brainstorming techniques and rules  Explain the rules of brainstorming  List and use the factors for effective brainstorming  Evaluate and practice good brainstorming technique  Utilize a checklist to ensure brainstorming sessions are optimal experiences    Duration:  2 hours    Target Audience:   Team Leaders, Managers and above    Additional Programs:  Creativity and Problem Solving, Innovation Tactics, Mind Mapping, Six Thinking Hats,

summary: This course provides an overview of the federal Universal Waste Rule. This rule provides generators with a more flexible approach for managing certain widely-generated, low-risk hazardous waste streams. The flexibility is intended to encourage resource conservation, as well as the diversion of universal wastes from landfills. The content in this course is designed to comply with the intent of the applicable regulatory requirements. Learner objectives are to identify the characteristics of batteries that make them a universal waste, identify basic handling requirements of lamps that qualify as universal waste, identify the hazardous waste items classified as universal waste under the Universal Waste Rule, identify the labeling and handling requirements of universal waste pesticides under the Universal Waste Rule, cite the requirements for the participants under the Universal Waste Rule, and cite the requirements for universal waste handlers under the Universal Waste Rule. Universal Waste Rule Training was developed with subject matter support provided by EnSafe Inc., a global professional services company focusing on engineering, environment, health and safety, and information technology. summary:
Achieving Agility  

The world of technology is evolving. Cryptocurrencies, self-driving cars, smarter phones, and virtual shopping are all pushing the world of technology faster and faster. Our clients, and therefore their projects, need to approach their projects in new ways so that they can respond quicker to changes in the marketplace and the regulatory landscape while keeping their customers engaged. By embracing new ways to deliver projects, we must manage those projects differently. Spending months collecting requirements and designing the "perfect" solution will become obsolete on Day One as the nature of the project shifts to account for the next technological innovation.   

To help you understand this new way of approaching projects, we are making available an Agile curriculum using a combination of virtual lessons and webinars to give you the knowledge necessary to become a Scrum Master and help our clients in this brave new world. The content will include: 

  • Overview of Agile 

  • Agile Values and Principles 

  • What is a Scrum Team? 

  • Sprinting without hurting yourself 

  • Writing good stories 

  • Managing the backlog   

These lessons, combined with a live webinar, will give you the material you need to take the Professional Scrum Master I (PSM I) certification exam and demonstrate your value to your clients and your project teams.

Course Full Name: Level 2 - Practitioners Certification in Quality Management System
summary:
Summary:

This certification program, provides an opportunity for team members to gain knowledge in Quality Management System. This certification program is mandatory for all team members in Application Services practice working in any Technology/Platform and are in Grades 8 and 9.

Objectives of this certification are to introduce, elucidate and provide robust understanding on necessary practices during project execution for an effective implementation.

  • Level 1 Synopsis - Summarize the modules covered as part of Level 1 – Practitioners Certification  in Quality Management System

  • Metrics and Measurement - Define Performance Objectives / Metrics required for the engagement in line with the type of work performed and sustain a measurement capability

  • Verification and Validation - Ensure deliverables to clients are reviewed and tested so that specified requirements are met

  • Causal Analysis and Resolution - Identify causes of problems/ issues/ variances/ deviations and take corrective action to improve performance of process and analyze positive outcomes

  • Requirements Management - Manage changes to requirements that contributes to carrying out impact analysis, firm up on changes required and estimate for the changes

  • Risk Management - Identify potential impacts to delivery before they occur so that risk handling activities can be planned and action taken for successful delivery

  • Decision Analysis and Resolution - Analyze possible solutions for a problem or a scenario using a formal evaluation process that results in identifying the most appropriate solution

  • Governance and Reviews - Understand the Governance and Review mechanism adopted from project kick-off to closure

  • Software Estimation - Predict most realistic amount of effort required to develop or maintain software based on specified inputs adopting different techniques

The process to obtain the certification is detailed below: 

  • Employees can enroll themselves for this NLCI Certification
  • All modules are mandated to be completed within a year
  • Certification Team will monitor and track the completion for Grades 8 and 9 team members for the year

Japanese young talent globalization program is an initiative by  headquarters where a batch of 12-15 selected Japanese employees will be visiting India once a quarter, to understand global business and particularly how we deliver to non-Japanese customers.  These selected employees are trained on communication and cross-border business before they visit India, which is the first phase.

 

The second phase of the program is organized in Bangalore which spans across 2 weeks. During their visit Japanese employees would be participating in certain field activities and also attending some class room sessions on topics specific to process, delivery etc.. to understand the business. The plan includes providing a buddy to each one of the Japanese participants during their visit to India, so as to facilitate exchange of ideas and to work together as a team in achieving the goal. We give an opportunity to Emerging Leaders and Gold Club members to play the role of buddy during this program.

summary:
Introduction:
The word DevOps is a contraction of 'Development' and 'Operations'. DevOps is a never-ending process of continuous improvement that can help increase the collaboration across Development and Operation to facilitate faster, more predictable and more frequent development releases to production environment.

The NTT Data Continuous Delivery framework for DevOps comprises of five key building blocks:

  • Continuous Requirements
  • Continuous Integration
  • Continuous Deployment
  • Continuous Testing and
  • Continuous Monitoring.

Employees of Grade 6 are required to complete career progression plan for Grade 6.

NTT DATA DevOps Competency building Framework:

NTT Data DevOps Competency Framework is owned by the DevOps Practice and specially designed to assist NTT DATA employees learn and advance their knowledge in DevOps. The objective is to help associates gain the basic competence required for specific roles.

Currently the framework addresses three levels aimed at specific audience:

  • Level 1 - Leaders/managers of current or prospective DevOps engagements
  • Level 2 - Software engineers in DevOps
  • Level 3 - Consultants or specialists in DevOps.


Target Audience for Level 1:

  • Leaders or Delivery Managers who are managing a Customer Engagement already providing or aspiring to provide services in DevOps
  • Software engineers involved or aspiring to take up DevOps roles


Objective for Level 1:
The objective of this Level -1 Certification is to provide the participants a high-level overview about the principles of DevOps. The content is prepared with the aim of introducing the phases, their significance and various tools used in each phase in the DevOps journey.  It will help the participants learn about DevOps ecosystem, continuous integration, containerization and automation concepts and how to deliver value to end customer through the software delivery process. All of this is expected to help the participants initiate, or further any conversations in progress, with their customers in their DevOps journey, and introduce NTT DATA's services in the same.  

Pre-requisites:
Exposure to engineering processes across different phases of Software Development Lifecycle and knowledge of the associated IT roles and responsibilities.

Process of Training:
Blended learning:  Self-paced eLearning and instructor-led clarification webinar sessions (as needed to supplement upon specific request).

Assessment method:
An online quiz at the end of the eLearning module

Summary:

Oracle APEX is a tool for building interactive, attractive web-based applications using SQL and PL/SQL code. It was developed by Oracle to provide a tool for developing applications with a minimum of programming efforts. Despite being a low code (or sometimes even no code) platform it still offers all kinds of customization options to enhance the framework.

APEX is a database centric framework hence it directly interacts with database hence reduce the database latency issues. APEX is also unique in that it offers flexibility in where it can be deployed. We can deploy

Oracle APEX on-premises, on the Oracle Cloud, on a private cloud, or anywhere else Oracle Database runs. Apart from above features, it also provides the various platform for community support.

 

This Oracle APEX basic (Level 1) certification course allows any NTT Developer to get basic idea about various properties of Oracle Application Express like Page, Reports, Forms, Creating an Application, User Roles, Security, etc.

Summary:
People Managers are expected to lead their team to success every single day. Their success is not an action by chance. It is focused efforts by optimally using time, resolving problems before they become conflicts. Hence, self-awareness for people managers on their time management habits, problem-solving approaches/strategies and conflict management modes becomes important. This module equips people managers on concepts of time management, practical approaches of problem solving and conflict management modes using a fine balance of scientific and management principles.

Pre-requisites:
DILO and case-studies to be completed before the session.

Intended Audience:
Grade 9 (People Managers) to 12.

Learning Objectives:

By the end of this session, participants will be able to:

  • Identify whether they are monochronic or polychronic managers,
  • Apply time management concepts to plan their activities for the day,
  • Assess their problem-solving skill,
  • Create practical approaches to problem solving using the conceptual framework shared in the session,
  • Identify their conflict management style, and
  • Regulate their conflict management approach to positively resolve problems/conflicts in a team

summary:
Purpose: To motivate NTT DATA employees to be intentional in self-evaluating verbal and non-verbal interactions with others and the consequences of those interactions to facilitate strong and supportive inclusive interpersonal relationships.

Learning Objectives:

  1. You will be able to recognize common sources of bias. 
  2. Learners will be equipped to perform self-evaluation of their perceptions of real-life experiences, including personal interactions, to determine the validity and accuracy of their perceptions by asking critical questions such as:
  • What is the basis for my perception?
  • What is the context of people and actions within a real-life experience?
  • Is my perception valid?
  • How might I normally react or respond to similar experiences?
  • Should I react or respond as usual, or differently?
  • What outcome do I expect from my response?
  • What was the outcome?
  • Do I need to change?
Course Description:
This course consists of an introduction to the course from our CEO, Bob Pryor, followed by a short video scenario and a high-level overview of the topic of unconscious bias.  When the video file is completed, you will need to complete a quiz to receive credit for course completion.  

The video scenario is a video produced by Bus Stop Films entitled, The Interviewer.  This short video gives us a view of unconscious bias in the workplace.  The characters are Thomas Howell, the interviewee; James Dexter, the interviewer; and Paul Dexter, James's father and employer.

Additional Information About "The Interviewer"
Bus Stop Films (BSF) is a pioneering, voluntarily run, not-for-profit organization based in Sydney, Australia.  They are dedicated to building the confidence, English skills, and life-ready skills of people with an intellectual disability and others from marginalized communities, through giving them access to a "film school" experience."  BSF currently works in partnership with the Australian Film Television and Radio School (AFTR) to deliver innovative and accessible film studies programs. They also advocate for more diversity and inclusion in the film industry. BSF was a finalist in the 2016 National Disability Awards and we won the 2016 Human Rights Award in the Community Organizationn Category.  You may wish to view a short video, The Making of the Interviewer.  

NTT DATA has made a generous donation to Bus Stop Films for the use of the video.  If you like and appreciate the work they are doing, you wish to make a personal donation of your own.  You may make a voluntary donation at https://www.busstopfilms.com.au/donate/.

Introduction:
GIT is the industry-standard software for distributed revision control and source code management system. GIT was initially designed and developed by Linus Torvalds for Linux kernel development. GIT is a free software distributed under the terms of the General Public License. With GIT, you can save snapshots of your work in a timeline. GIT allows you to create backups that take minimum space, making workspace safer. 

Employees of Grade 6 are required to complete career progression plan for Grade 6.

NTT DATA DevOps Competency building Framework:
NTT Data DevOps Competency Framework is owned by the DevOps Practice and specially designed to assist NTT DATA employees learn and advance their knowledge in DevOps. The objective is to help associates gain the basic competence required for specific roles.

Currently the framework addresses three levels aimed at specific audience:

  • Level 1 - Leaders/managers of current or prospective DevOps engagements
  • Level 2 - Software engineers in DevOps
  • Level 3 - Consultants or specialists in DevOps.


Target Audience for Level 2:
Software engineers involved or aspiring to take up DevOps roles, this course help beginners learn the basic functionality of GIT version control system.

Objective for Level 2:
The objective of this Level -2 Certification is to provide the participants a high-level overview about the source code management. The motive of GIT is to manage a project or a set of files as they change over time. GIT stores this information in a data structure called a GIT repository. The repository is the core of GIT. The content is prepared with the aim of introducing the GIT theory and the workflow, Repositories and what they are, Basic and Advanced GIT commands

Pre-requisites:
Exposure to engineering processes across different phases of Software Development Lifecycle and knowledge on using your preferred OS.

Process of Training:
Blended learning:  Self-paced eLearning and instructor-led clarification webinar sessions (as needed to supplement upon specific request).

Assessment method:
An online quiz at the end of the eLearning module

summary:

summary:
Summary

Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA) is a Federal law passed by US Congress in August, 1996.

The “Health Insurance Portability” (HIP) part of HIPAA was intended to ensure the continuity of health insurance coverage for workers changing jobs. To facilitate this goal, Congress mandated national standards for transmitting and protecting health information.

The “Accountability” part of HIPAA was designed to ensure the security and confidentiality of patient information / data and requires uniform standards for electronic transmission of data relating to patient health information.

The Big Data Developer Certification Program provides a structured assessment to measure and certify the competency level of developers in Big Data technology. It has been developed by the Big Data Practice team based on the Generic Capability Building Certification Framework.  It consists of the following e-learning modules.

E-Learning

HBase

Percipio

  • Introduction to Apache Spark
  • Spark Monitoring & Tuning
  • Apache Spark SQL
  • Spark Security

Percipio

  • Getting Started with Hive
  • Loading & Querying Data with Hive

  • Solr Queries

Percipio

  • Apache Kafka: Concepts & Components
  • Apache Kafka: Deployment & Operating Tasks
  • Apache Kafka: Operations
  • Apache Kafka: Development

Percipio

 

Pre-requisites:

Employees aspiring for Big Data Developer Certification program are expected to have basic knowledge in Java, Linux and/or Python.

Enrolment and certification process:

Employees pursuing the Certification should follow these steps –

  1. Complete all the courses listed above (self-paced learning)
  2. After completion send an email to Big Data Practice (IDS-Certification@nttbigdata.com) copying their HLM with a request to enroll for the Certification
  3. HLM’s will review and send their approval/rejection to the Practice
  4. Practice will review the nominations and send an assignment along with the instructions for accessing a cloud based environment for working on the assignment, to the employees selected for each batch
  5. Employees must complete the assignment per the instructions provided and submit within the stipulated time
  6. Practice will assess the submitted assignments and call for a viva voce to evaluate
  7. Qualified employees will be awarded the Big Data Developers Certification.

The overarching goal is to help prepare attendees for working in Scrum delivery or supporting the Scrum teams as they execute in the Scrum framework.

During this two-day course attendees will gain an in-depth understanding of the Scrum framework, as well as an in-depth understanding of the Agile Manifesto principles and values, and how the manifesto serves as a foundation for Scrum. The course is designed to distinguish between waterfall delivery and Scrum delivery; and includes an in-depth exploration of key roles, events, process, artifacts, and metrics. Attendees will learn how to write stories and break down features, plan and execute Sprints, and effectively use estimation techniques. They will also be introduced to Kanban - how its featured in Scrum and how it helps power the framework. Finally, attendees will briefly learn about the continuous delivery pipeline and DevOps culture, how to effectively integrate with other teams in a cross-team program.

SAP NetWeaver Master Data Management is a component of SAP's NetWeaver product group and is used as a platform to consolidate, cleanse and synchronise a single version of the truth for master data within a heterogeneous application landscape.

Learning Objectives:
SAP MDM is used to manage and distribute the different master data used in SAP Primarily Material Master, Customer Master, Vendor Master.  And that's exactly what SAP MDM tries to resolve through its Netweaver technology platform.

Topics Covered:

Introduction to SAP NetWeaver Technology

  • Starting and stopping MDM console
  • Mounting and un Mounting MDM server
  • Connecting to MDM server.
  • Creating MDM repository.
  • Creating Different Tables.
  • Creating Different Fields.
  • Working with users, roles, remote system and ports.


MDM data Manager

  • Working with five different modes.
  • CURD operations
  • Search techniques
  • Assignments and validations
  • Workflow
  • Matching
  • Qualified table
  • Hierarchy table
  • Taxonomy table


MDM import Manager

  • Importing different source data(Excel, Access and xml)
  • Importing from multiple tables
  • Different operations on source table.
  • Source mapping and value mapping.
  • Matching of records.
  • Creating Maps
  • Using created Maps


MDM Syndicate

  • Syndicating single table data
  • Syndicating data with external source
  • Syndication data to XML and Flat source
  • Creating custom fields.
  • Working with MAPs
  • Working with Import Server
  • Working with Syndicate Server

Prerequisites:
MDM server installed

  • Four GUI’s of MDM is Console, Data Manager, Syndicator, Import manager
  • A Data base like oracle

Intended Audience:
SAP consultants

Mode of Learning:
Recordings

Course Full Name: Logic in Writing, Thinking and Problem Solving
summary:
If you want to build credibility with your clients or get the attention of potential new clients, then you need to master a critical skill beyond work ethic: the ability to communicate more information, more clearly, in a limited amount of time.  As a consultant, you might only have a few minutes to get your point across before a busy executive stop paying attention to you. If you fail to get right to the point, you risk losing them.


Logic in Writing, Thinking and Problem Solving is based on a principle that allows you to quickly seize your audience’s attention and communicate with gravitas, by creating a compelling story that is easy to understand and remember.

 

Learn problem solving strategies (SCQA Process) that will help you separate the thinking from the doing and will help you turn a mountain of seemingly complex information into something that will begin to make sense. Sharpen your communication skills by starting with the answer and focus on getting to the point, or the “bottom line,” then support your answer with underlying arguments and data.

Building a Culture of Accountability and Transparency
summary:
Everyone makes mistakes. It’s inevitable since it’s part of being human. But after you’ve made a mistake, you have a choice.

  • Take the right action by being accountable, owning up to the mistake and taking corrective action. With this approach, you learn from the mistake which can prevent similar mistakes in the future.
  • Or take the easy way out by denying and covering up the mistake. This invariably worsens the situation. Also, there are no lessons learned and you risk making the same mistake again.


We have created a learning module comprising of scenarios that you encounter regularly. In each scenario an unintentional mistake can possibly happen. By covering the mistake, the issue gets out of hand. But by owning the mistake and acting with accountability and transparency, the issue gets resolved.

Attendees can improve collaboration and alignment in a SAFe® Lean-Agile enterprise when they become a SAFe 5 Architect. The SAFe® for Architects course prepares System, Solution, and Enterprise Architects to engage across the organization as effective leaders and change agents who collaboratively deliver architectural solutions.

During this three-day course, attendees will explore the roles, responsibilities, and mindset of Agile Architects, and appreciate how to align architecture with business value and drive continuous flow to large systems-of-systems while supporting SAFe program execution.

This course is for senior technical contributors who need to understand the role of System, Solution, and Enterprise Architects in Lean-Agile enterprises. The course is also appropriate for individuals desiring a deeper view into how architecture enables continuous value flow and how architects engage in, and contribute to, a Lean-Agile enterprise.

Sessions are held over 4 days at 5-6 hours per day. Please see schedule for details. 

THIS COURSE REQUIRES MANAGER APPROVAL TO SIGN-UP.

NOTE: Cost for this US-led course is $676, and cost for the India-led course is $438.  Please confirm with your manager before signing up.  After class completion, either the Cost Center or WBS will be charged based on the manager’s prior approval.


Learners taking this course are:

Architect, Solution Architect, System Architect, Scrum Master, Agile Coach, Consultant, Agile Trainer


Topics Covered

• Exemplifying Lean-Agile architecture

• Architecting for DevOps and Release on Demand

• Aligning architecture with business value

• Developing Solution Vision, Solution Intent, and Roadmaps

• Preparing architecture for Program Increment (PI) Planning

• Coordinating architecture throughout PI Planning

• Supporting Continuous Delivery during PI execution

• Supporting new Strategic Themes and Value Streams

• Leading as an architect during a Lean-Agile transformation

Course Information

What Attendees Get

The class registration includes:

• Attendee workbooks

• Eligibility to take the SAFe® 5 Architect (ARCH) exam1

• One-year membership to the SAFe Community Platform

• Course certificate of completion

Prerequisites

The following prerequisites are highly recommended:

• Have attended at least one SAFe course

• Have participated in at least one ART and one PI

Exam Details

Completion of this course gives you access to the exam and all related study materials as part of your Learning Plan in the SAFe Community Platform.

For more information about the exam and benefits of becoming a Certified SAFe professional, click the More Exam Details button.

Course Summary:

This certification program, provides an opportunity for team members to gain knowledge in advanced AS/400 programming concepts, which would be useful to work on all types AS/400 based projects. This certification program is for all team members in Application Services practice working on any AS/400 Projects and are in Grades 5 and above.  We encourage other team members too to take up this AS/400 Level 2 certification.

Learning Objectives:
In this module, you will gain knowledge in below topics:

  • Sub Files concepts : In this module you will learn about Subfile Overview, Various Types of Subfiles and their loading techniques, Message Subfile etc.
  • Printer Files concepts : In this module you will learn about printer files, how we design a printer file and the printer file keywords.
  • Embedded SQL : In this module you will learn about  Embedded SQL, Communication Area, Embedded SQL Statements and types of SQL, Cursors and types, creation steps of Embedded SQL and Keywords.
  • RPG ILE concepts : ILE RPG is an implementation of the RPG IV language on the IBM® i with the IBM i operating system. This module is for programmers who are familiar with the RPG programming language, but who want to learn how to use it in the ILE framework. This provides a detailed description of the RPG IV language.

Pre-requisites:
Employees must have basic AS/400 programming knowledge & work experience on AS/400 projects. Employees are also expected to completed AS/400 Level 1 certification, prior to starting of this certification.

Intended Audience:
Grade 5 and Grade 6 resources.

Mode of Learning:
e-Learning modules

Mode of Assessment:
Online Quiz

Summary:
SAP Business Planning and Consolidation (BPC) tool is used to support all operational and financial activities also helps in automating and streamlining business planning, budgeting, forecasting, & consolidation activities of the organization. This toll helps in establishing sales, CAPEX, OPEX, Revenue, etc. types planning scenarios.

The topics covered are as follows: 

  • Purpose of BPC, System architecture, BW/BPC objects, Versions/Roadmap, Landscape & Features /key benefits
  • BPC Modelling (How to create Environment, Dimensions, Models, Interfaces (EPM, Web, SAP GUI), Security)
  • Master & Transaction data loading 
  • Crating Data manager packages, transformation & Conversion files. 
  • Creating Reports & Input schedules 
  • Using Script Logic & dimension Member formulas  
  • Creation and use of Business rules 
  • Different Planning types/Functions
  • Work status & BPF's 
  • Controls & Audit reports 
  • Types of consolidation & modelling 
  • Creation of Rates, Ownership, Consolidation Models
  • Consolidation Methods 
  • Inter Company Matchings and Adjustments
  • Inter Company/US Eliminations
  • Currency conversion 
  • Account reclassification & Journal Template
  • SAP BPC 10.1 NetWeaver Embedded on HANA
  • SAP BPC Optimized for S/4HANA.
  • Reporting on AFO
  • BPC-Tickets/Incident Management Support System
  • Overview of SAP SAC & PaPM


Learning Objectives:

The objective of this course is to have a comprehensive idea about the Planning process and Consolidation process in SAP BPC. 

  • To know how to use the tool for different types modelling for different types of planning scenarios also to understand the consolidation setup to be executed. 
  • This course will teach how to create templates and reports.

Prerequisites:

  • Good knowledge in SAP BW objects and process. 
  • Good functional knowledge in functional side of the business (FICO) & good analytical and statistical knowledge. Moderate knowledge in MDX language for scripting. 

Intended Audience:
From Grade 5 to 8 Employees in NTT DATA.

Mode of Learning:
E-learning

Duration:
14.67 Hrs

Summary:
The Payment Medium Workbench (PMW) is a tool used to configure and create payment media in particular formats which are not available in standard payment medium programs (RFFO*).

DMEE (Data Medium Exchange):
DME Stands for ‘Data Medium Exchange’. The function of DME Administration is to create documents in file form. For This it uses DME Engine to define the Structure of file. DMEEngine enables you to define your Particular local format yourself without any ABAP programming knowledge or coding.

Configuration Steps Detail;-

Create / Copy an existing PM format. T Code: OBPM1

Enter data related to format output

Enter data related to format Information

Enter data related to Program Control

Enter data related to Grouping

Create / Copy a New Function tree

Function Tree ........Enter DME Properties………………Admin Data

Function Tree ..........Enter DME Properties………………Format Attributes

Function Tree .........Enter DME Properties………………Levels

Function Tree ........Enter DME Properties………………Sort

Function Tree ..Creating Nodes………………….Segment Group

Function Tree ............................Create Segments

Function Tree.......... Add Data Fields……………..Constants

Function Tree...............Add Data Fields……………..Structure field

Function Tree.............Add Data Fields……………..Aggregations

Function Tree.............Conditions

Function Tree..................... Check & Activate

Assign PM format to Payment method

Creating Variant……TCode : OBPM4

Execute APP……..

                Learning Objectives:

                The objective of this course is to have a comprehensive idea about the Configuration process of DMEE in SAP.

                Prerequisites:
                Good business process understanding in Finance and Controlling and understand the accounting terminology and the accounting flow. Apart from this you need to understand the logic how the data is flowing from various modules to FICO module in the SAP system.

                Intended Audience:
                From Grade 5 to 8 Employees in NTT DATA.

                Mode of Learning:
                E-learning

                Duration:
                 2 Hrs

summary:
Summary :
In this course, we will learn about OpenStack and its fundamentals as well as services such as OpenStack Object Storage, OpenStack Compute, OpenStack Networking, OpenStack Metering, and OpenStack Block Storage, to name a few.

We will, moreover, discuss the Bare Metal service, which provides components that can be used to provision and manage physical machines for end-users, along with the Deployment architecture and Logical architecture of a Bare Metal service in OpenStack.

In this course, we’ll go through the concepts of Red Hat OpenStack Platform and its architecture. Launch OpenStack instances using Docker machine, run Kubernetes clusters for orchestration and learn about several tools that can be used to manage OpenStack deployment and lifecycle.

You will learn how to launch an instance of an application component, install and configure Jenkins automation servers and the process of setting up Vagrant to start an OpenStack AIO node.

We also cover the processes of managing compute nodes, integration of identity management and managing OpenStack user security.

You will also get to learn how Horizon dashboard works and work with OpenStack CLI client along with troubleshooting processes. 

CEPH
Through this course, we will expose the challenges that traditional storage faces and how Ceph fixes them, as well as how Ceph stores data with Pools. 

We will examine how to install Ceph with Proxmox and discuss how Proxmox provides High Availability; and in addition, explore Pools and Placement Groups and demonstrate working with Placement Groups and creating backups with Proxmox. 

We will also be delving into the CRUSH Algorithm, which is in charge of controlling scalable decentralized application data placement, along with POOL, PG, and CRUSH. 

This course will also explain how to manage the monitor and OSD maps to maintain cluster operation, quorum, and consistency, and identify key performance metrics for a Ceph cluster and use them to help tune and troubleshoot the operating system and Ceph software for optimal performance. 

We will as well look at various methods of troubleshooting Clusters, such as cluster performance troubleshooting of CPU, Memory, and Block devices and cluster performance troubleshooting of Networks.


Prerequisite :

  • Linux- It is the most essential prerequisite for OpenStack. As OpenStack itself is deployed on Linux environment, you need to have a good understanding of Linux. It helps you to debug, troubleshoot issues faster. Any configuration changes will be easy if you know how Linux works.
  • Reference URL: https://www.linux.org/forums/linux-beginner-tutorials.123/
  • Networking - As the cloud environment is entirely linked to networking, you need to have good knowledge of VLAN, VXLAN, GRE, L2, L3 networking, OVS and Linux Bridges.
  • Hypervisors - You need to know what a hypervisor is and how it functions. KVM and ESXi will be good enough.
  • If you want to be an OpenStack developer, you number one prerequisite would be python, as the entire OpenStack is written on Python.
  • Reference URl: https://wiki.python.org/moin/BeginnersGuide
  • OpenStack Documentation: https://docs.openstack.org/openstack-ansible/latest/user/aio/quickstart.html
  • VMs will run on UBUNTU 16.04 Linux (Ubuntu Xenial)
  • Good Internet Connectivity
  • For single AIO node setup
    • 64 bit OS
    • Mac or Windows computer with 6GB free RAM, 10 GB free disk & 2 CPU Cores

  • For single Multi node setup

    • 64 bit OS
    • Mac or Windows computer 9 GB Free RAM, 12 GB free HD & 2 CPU Cores

CEPH

  • Basic understanding of command line utilities and storage principles.
  • Basic experience with Linux.
  • Ceph documentation: https://docs.ceph.com/en/pacific/
  • Linix documentation: https://linux.die.net/

Learning Objectives:
Detailed knowledge of OpenStack, Red Hat curriculum and CEPH concept.

Learn the NTT DATA policy for internally and externally developed software.

Understand what software development costs can be capitalized.

Learn which general ledger accounts must be used to record software costs in SAP and why it’s important to use the correct general ledger account.

The Certifications are designed to provide knowledge of the U.S. HealthCare industry, insights on transforming the business environment, and knowledge of some of the key processes (e.g., Accounts Receivable Management, Claims Adjudication). 

The Certification program has three levels: Basic, Intermediate and Advanced. The courses are mapped to the levels based on complexity and immensity, and in a generic-to-specific order.

All courses are available in the form of highly interactive eLearning modules to enable self-paced learning and completion.

Benefits:
This program provides comprehensive knowledge of the HealthCare domain, covering broad spectrum of topics.

It orients the learner to various scenarios in some of the key areas of Revenue Cycle Management (RCM) / HealthCare payments ecosystem, and related resolution procedures.

The contextual knowledge gained from this program serves as a foundation to build competencies and skills related to BPO Delivery and Operations.

Eligibility Criteria:
Non-BPO team members:

  • Open to all team members.

BPO team members:

  • Open to all team members in grade 5 and above.
  • Team members in grades 3 and 4 with tenure >1.5 year are eligible.

To enrol to intermediate and advanced levels, the team members must complete the preceding level(s).

How to enrol and additional information

  • Request for enrolment is to be raised through the Employee Service Center (ESC) tool. Select ‘’Service Category’’ as ‘’Training and Development’’. Then select ‘’Incident Category’’ as ‘’Certification”.
  • An E-certificate will be awarded upon successful completion of each level.

The course covers basics of different protocols used in different infrastructure applications and for interoperability to augment admin tasks. It covers fundamentals of IT, networks, and Unified communication & collaboration (also referred to as IP telephony)

Pre-requisites:
Basic knowledge of computers

Learning Objectives:

The objective is to train freshers, associates and the professionals who have started their career, to familiarize them with networking and IP telephony. It will equip them with the information needed to troubleshoot unified communications issues which are independent of vendor technologies.

This course can also be used by professionals who have worked only on IP telephony to cross train them with interoperable technologies to help them troubleshoot day to day issues with network and telephony.

Course Summary: 

The Product Management Foundational Certification introduces you to the concept of product management, skills, and knowledge required to successfully manage a portfolio of applications by applying product management concepts and principles, viewing each system or application as a “product.”

Over the years, as clients continue to transform their application portfolio in line with their digital transformation programs, the approach to Application Management has also evolved to embrace the principles of Agile, DevOps, and ITIL 4 to deliver application management services. You will also get an overview of Application Management Services (AMS), the Conscious Enterprise Services (CES) framework, and the Continuous Modernization of AMS.

Sustainability is on the cusp of an evolutionary leap. Companies all over the world are beginning to explore more sustainable ways of doing business, primarily due to the global

climate emergency. They consider their long-term impact on the local environment, society,

and the economy and ask whether their business makes a positive contribution. Becoming

more sustainable may not be easy at first, but business sustainability is more an opportunity than a threat. Sustainable companies will be more resilient and will create an enduring impact.
